page.layout: One printed page (left-hand page of the opening, the right-hand strip is the neighbouring page's edge and is not transcribed). Running head at top centre. Main text in one column, with a marginal note at the left margin beside the first lines. Catchword at lower right of the column.

main_text.p: sese vere habeant, quis sanationem, factam per unguentum armarium, quo vulnus etiam non applicatis remediis curatur, instrumento tantum eo unguento delibuto, non naturale, sed superstitiosam dicet & impostoriam? Nemo sane, nisi harum rerum omnium ignarus, quique sensibus omnia metitur. Fit enim illa sanatio per meram naturam atque magneticam quandam efficientiam, attractionem & deductionem, per influentiam corporum coelestium operationes suas perficientium per elementa, nec non toties decantatum vectorem Spiritum, qui tanquam medium vinculum primo ex definitis & propriis constellationibus sympathiam, & copulam seu conuenientiam inducit, ex qua deinceps vis sanatoria in telum medicatum deriuatur, unde postea egreditur, & ad partem usque vulneratam continuatur ac traducitur, tandemque actionem istius virtutis Spiritualis consequitur effectus. Nec tamen dubium, phantasiam patientis plurimum hic habere momenti, (iuxta illud Hippocratis, in medendo saepe concurrunt spes, fiducia & τύχη) tum ad balsamicam in sanguine existentem virrutem a telo medicato attrahendam dirigendamque ad partem affectam & laesam, tum ad movendum principium sanatiuum, id est, sanandi virtute praeditum, in corpore existens. Coelum igitur, quod pluri-
main_text.head: pluri-
main_text.p: Modus quo vulnus curatur sine remediis.

page.notes: Marginal note at left: "Modus quo vulnus curatur sine remediis." Its text is in italic. Right-hand strip is the edge of the facing page and is not transcribed. The word "pluri-" at the foot is the catchword, not a heading; the final line in the main text is printed as a catchword and should be read only as such. Some letters in the scan are faint (e.g. "phantasiam", "virrutem") and may be misread.
